source.authors: Matzrafi M, Raz H, Rubin B, Yaacoby T, Eizenberg H
source.title: Distribution and Biology of the Invasive Weed Parthenium hysterophorus L. in Israel

method: plants grown under black shading net giving 0 (full natural light, 1,000 to 1,100 umol m-2 s-1), 30, 60 and 90% shading; height, flowers and aboveground biomass recorded weekly on five plants and a log-logistic curve fitted per shading level
where: full article text, Frontiers in Agronomy 3: 639991 (frontiersin.org/journals/agronomy/articles/10.3389/fagro.2021.639991/full), abstract, Methods and Results read over four fetches; the page prints that the article is open access under the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY); Crossref gives CC BY 4.0, volume 3, article 639991, published 14 June 2021, and no issue
value: under induced shading of 60 and 90%, a significant reduction in biomass, height and number of flowers per plant was observed
conditions: net house in Israel in the natural growing season (May to July); 50 plants per treatment; seeds pooled from 30 to 40 plants at one site (Newe Ya'ar), collected November 2015; one population only. Results figures (maximal values of per-level fitted curves; Tables 3 to 5): shoot biomass 28 g at 0% shading, 24.2 g at 30%, 16.1 g at 60%, 2.3 g at 90%; maximal height 128.9 cm at 0%, 88.8 cm at 30%, 77.2 cm at 60%, 2.6 to 6 cm at 90% (plants did not bolt); maximal flowers per plant 71.1 at 0%, 81.5 at 30%, 42.1 at 60%, none at 90% (flower initiation did not occur). The abstract names only 60 and 90% as significant reductions; the paper gives no direct test of 30% against 0% (each level has its own fitted curve), and at 30% flowering was higher than at 0% (see the paired 30% record); the paper's '13%' is 14.7% above the 0% level by the Table 5 values (71.045 and 81.472) and matches the gap as a share of the 30% value; the paper reports no test between any two shading levels, so 'significant' rests on each fitted curve's own P-values; the 90% height of 2.6 to 6 cm is the text's range (Table 4 gives 4.72 cm); plants grew in 2.5 L pots and the run is not described as repeated
quote: Our results show that under induced shading of 60 and 90%, a significant reduction in biomass, height, and a number of flowers per plant were observed.
note: Full text read; the abstract sentence is whole, reassembled from two consecutive fetch segments that were confirmed on a second fetch. Germination light/dark was not tested in this paper. Accepted name: POWO powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:236510-1 (opened) Parthenium hysterophorus L. 'This species is accepted'; WFO wfoplantlist.org/taxon/wfo-0000065156-2022-06 (opened) accepted, id wfo-0000065156 (June 2022 snapshot, flagged older classification; the 2025-06 page was blocked by the fetch permission step and a newer snapshot could not be tried).

where: full article text, Frontiers in Agronomy 3: 639991 (frontiersin.org/journals/agronomy/articles/10.3389/fagro.2021.639991/full), abstract, Methods and Results read over four fetches; the page prints that the article is open access under the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY); Crossref gives CC BY 4.0, volume 3, article 639991, published 14 June 2021, and no issue
value: at 30% shading the maximal flowers per plant was higher than at 0% shading, by 13% (a contrary result to the reduction at 60 and 90%); no statistical test of this difference is reported
conditions: net house in Israel in the natural growing season (May to July); 50 plants per treatment; one population (Newe Ya'ar, collected November 2015). Results figures (maximal values of per-level fitted curves; Tables 3 to 5): shoot biomass 28 g at 0% shading, 24.2 g at 30%, 16.1 g at 60%, 2.3 g at 90%; maximal height 128.9 cm at 0%, 88.8 cm at 30%, 77.2 cm at 60%, 2.6 to 6 cm at 90% (plants did not bolt); maximal flowers per plant 71.1 at 0%, 81.5 at 30%, 42.1 at 60%, none at 90% (flower initiation did not occur). Fitted maxima of flowers per plant (the 'a' parameter of Table 5) are 71.045 at 0% and 81.472 at 30%; the text gives no direct statistical test of 30% against 0%, and biomass and height at 30% are lower than at 0% (24.2 against 28 g; 88.8 against 128.9 cm), also without a direct test; the paper's '13%' is 14.7% above the 0% level by the Table 5 values (71.045 and 81.472) and matches the gap as a share of the 30% value; the paper reports no test between any two shading levels, so 'significant' rests on each fitted curve's own P-values; the 90% height of 2.6 to 6 cm is the text's range (Table 4 gives 4.72 cm); plants grew in 2.5 L pots and the run is not described as repeated
quote: Total flowering was higher by 13% for the 30% shading in comparison with the 0% shading level as presented by the a parameter (maximum flowering) in Table 5.
note: Full text read; quote is the whole Results sentence, reassembled from two consecutive fetch segments, both seen in two fetches. The preceding sentence reads 'For both 0 and 30% shading, the maximal amount of flowers per plant was 71.1 and 81.5, respectively (Table 5).'
